units.text: This section defines the features and functional operations of Base Die Buffering (BDB) DRAM package.
units.raw_text: This section defines the features and functional operations of Base Die Buffering (BDB) DRAM package.

style_runs.text: This section defines the features and functional operations of Base Die Buffering (BDB) DRAM package.

units.text: DDR6 can support BDB DRAM which is desinged for high-density multi-die stacked package, facilitating reduced load on CK, CS, CA, and DQ/DQS signals for improved singal integrity as well as lower power relative to unbuffered DRAM package.
units.raw_text:
DDR6 can 
support BDB DRAM which is desinged for high-density multi-die stacked package, facilitating reduced load on CK, 
CS, CA, and DQ/DQS signals for improved singal integrity as well as lower power relative to unbuffered DRAM 
package.

style_runs.text: support BDB DRAM which is desinged for high-density multi-die stacked package, facilitating reduced load on CK,
CS, CA, and DQ/DQS signals for improved singal integrity as well as lower power relative to unbuffered DRAM

units.text: In multi-rank package, unbuffered DRAM has multiple indipendent DRAM dies wire bonded together, increasing electrical loading on the system channels.
units.raw_text:
In multi-rank package, unbuffered DRAM has multiple indipendent DRAM dies wire bonded together, increasing 
electrical loading on the system channels.

style_runs.text: In multi-rank package, unbuffered DRAM has multiple indipendent DRAM dies wire bonded together, increasing
electrical loading on the system channels.

units.text: The BDB DRAM technology mitigates this with the “Base DRAM Die” (hereinafter “Base Die”) being a single electrical load, exclusively interfacing the memory controller for the stacked DRAM package no matter if the stack height is 2, 4, or 8.
units.raw_text:
The BDB DRAM technology mitigates this with the “Base DRAM Die” 
(hereinafter “Base Die”) being a single electrical load, exclusively interfacing the memory controller for the stacked 
DRAM package no matter if the stack height is 2, 4, or 8.

style_runs.text: The BDB DRAM technology mitigates this with the “Base DRAM Die”
(hereinafter “Base Die”) being a single electrical load, exclusively interfacing the memory controller for the stacked
DRAM package no matter if the stack height is 2, 4, or 8.

units.text: One or more vertically stacked “Core DRAM Dies” (hereinafter “Core Dies”) are directly connected to the Base Die through die-to-die interconnects within the package.
units.raw_text:
One or more vertically stacked “Core DRAM Dies” (here-
inafter “Core Dies”) are directly connected to the Base Die through die-to-die interconnects within the package.

style_runs.text: One or more vertically stacked “Core DRAM Dies” (here-
inafter “Core Dies”) are directly connected to the Base Die through die-to-die interconnects within the package.

units.text: This topology isolates external IO between the host and the base die and internal IO between the base die and core dies, improving memory subsystem SI and saving power from Core Dies by turning off redundant IO circuit blocks mainly built for external communications.
units.raw_text:

improving memory subsystem SI and saving power from Core Dies by turning off redundant IO circuit blocks mainly 
built for external communications.

cells.text: RESET: Reset is active when RESET_n is LOW, and inactive when RESET_n is HIGH. RESET_n must be HIGH during normal operation. RESET_n is an asynchronous signal.

Clock: CK_t and CK_c are differential clock inputs. The first crossing point is the rising (falling) edge of CK_t (CK_c) and second crossing point is falling (rising) edge of CK_t (CK_c). Command/Address and CS inputs are sampled on the crossing point that is the rising (falling) edge of CK_t (CK_c). One CK_t and CK_c pair are shared for both pseudo-split die (PSD0, PSD1).

Chip Select: CS is part of the command code, the pulse width is 2CK and is sampled on the even rising (falling) edge of CK_t (CK_c) unless the device is in power-down mode where it becomes an asynchronous signal. All commands are masked when CS is registered LOW.

Command/Address Inputs: CA signals provide the command and address inputs according to the Command Truth Table. Note: Since some commands are multi-cycle, the pins may not be interchanged between devices on the same bus.

Data Strobe: DQS_t and DQS_c are the differential output clock signals used to strobe data during a READ and differential input clock signals used to latch WRITE data. The differential crossing point is edge-aligned with READ data and centered for WRITE data. One DQS_t and DQS_c pair are shared for both pseudo-split die (PSD0, PSD1).
ALERT: If an error is detected and reported to the fault register, the ALERT encodes the type of error on the pin. See the Alert section for details.
ZQ: ZQ is used to calibrate the output drive strength and the termination resistance as calibration reference. There is one ZQ pad per die.
Power supplies: Isolated on the die for improved noise immunity. Includes the main power, DQ power and row activation power.
Ground Reference: Power supply ground reference.
No Connect: No internal electrical connection is present.

NOTE 3: There are two physical registers assigned to each bit of this MR parameter, designated set point 0 and set point 1. Please refer to TBD section for more information on FSP operation. NOTE 4: The time required for VREFCA to reach the set level depends on the step size from the current level to the new level. See TBD for more information on VREFCA training. NOTE 5: VREFCA can be adjusted by either MRW(MR84[6:0]) in normal mode (not MRUPDATE mode) or VREF_CA shadow register with VREFCA Apply Functional Mode (MR06[3]=1B) in MRUPDATE mode. NOTE 6: Control of VREFCA during CATM is referred to section 4.2.8 (CATM) NOTE 7: Refer to Table 2 for the detailed VREFCA setting values.

NOTE 1: These values may be used for MR1A84[6:0] to set the VREFCA levels in the DDR6 SDRAM. NOTE 2: Absolute VREFCA low level (%code * VDDQ) must be higher than or equal to 75mV for normal operation. VREFCA error is not included this calculation. NOTE 3: Absolute VREFCA high level (%code * VDDQ) must be lower than or equal to VREFCA max, which refers to values in Table xx (CA Rx mask specification), for normal operation. VREFCA error is not included this calculation. NOTE 4: VREFCA codes from 0000000B to 0000100B are able to be used only for testing purpose not for normal operation. VREFCA accuracy are not guaranteed from 0000000B to 0000100B. NOTE 5: The VREFCA codes from 1110010B to 1111111B are provided to support cases where VDDQ is lower than the typical value, enabling the absolute VREFCA value to reach 0.4V.When VDDQ is at its typical voltage, codes with an absolute VREFCA value of higher than 0.4V cannot be used. This restriction also applies during training operations. NOTE 6: The default VREFCA is defined by CA ODT strap value.

They are defined by the states of CS of clocks pairs C0/C1, C2/C3, C4/C5, and by the states of CA[54:0] of clocks C0, C1, C2, C3, C4, C5. CS is 2N pulse width and center aligned to clocks C0, C2 and C4. CS is “Don’t Care” at clocks C1, C3, and C5. In CA 2N mode, the CS shall operate identically to CA 1N mode and the command lengths shall be doubled relative to 1N mode, corresponding to four (4), eight (8) or twelve (12) clock cycles long. NOTE 1: DRAM vendors must report all of the possible settings over the operating temperature range of the device. Each vendor guarantees that their device will work at any temperature within the range using the refresh interval requested by their device. NOTE 2: The 2x Refresh Rate must be provided by the system before the DRAM Tj has gone up by more than 2°C (Temperature Margin) since the first report out of MR04[2:0]=100. This condition is reset when MR04[2:0] is equal to 011. NOTE 3: The device may not operate properly when MR04[2:0]=110 and the DRAM Tj has gone up by more than 2 °C (Temperature Margin) since the first report out of MR04[2:0]=110. This condition is reset when MR04[2:0] is equal to 101. MR04[2:0]=110 must be a temporary condition of the DRAM, to be addressed by immediately reducing the Tj of the DRAM by throttling its power, and/or the power of nearby devices. NOTE 4: MR04[4] = 0 at power-up. MR04[2:0] bits are valid after initialization sequence (Te). NOTE 5: When MR04[4]=1, the refresh rate reported in MR04[2:0] has changed since the last MR04 read. A mode register read from MR04 will reset MR04[4] to '0'. NOTE 6: MR04[2:0] bits indicate the latest Refresh Rate whenever MR04[4] = 1 NOTE 7: See the section on “Temperature Sensor” for information on the recommended frequency of reading MR04 NOTE 8: The two PSDs (PSD0 and PSD1) on a single die share the same thermal sensor, therefore the thermal offset value in MR04[7:5] is applied to the common thermal sensor

In blocking mode only, the DRAM shall delay the erroneous command by PL and then ignore it.

In both blocking and nonblocking modes, log the error by storing the erroneous command and address bits in the CA Parity Error Log C0-C5 mode registers for the PSD with the error. The DRAM maintains the CA Parity Error Log C0-C5 mode registers for the first erroneous command until the CA Parity Error Status mode register bit is cleared to 0.

Set the CA Parity Error Status bit in the mode register to ‘1’. The CA Parity Error Status bit must be setbefore tCMD_BLOCKING finishes within (tPAR_ALERT_ON + tMRD). The CA Parity Error Status bit remains 1 until the host clears it explicitly using an MRW command or MRUPDATE Mode.
All in-progress commands shall continue without interruption.

In blocking modeonly, the DRAM shall ignore subsequent commands immediately after the erroneous command on the same PSD’s CA bus and shall continue to ignore commands on the same PSD’s CA bus until after tCMD_BLOCKING.

If the Alert State Enable on CA Parity Error mode register bit is 1,Assert the ALERT signal to the host within tPAR_ALERT_ON time for tPAR_ALERT_PW. After tPAR_ALERT_PW has been satisfied, the DRAM shall de-assert ALERT.

In nonblocking mode only, disable DQS outputs starting between tPAR_ALERT_ON and (RL - tRPRE) after the erroneous command and keep the DQS outputs disabled until after tCMD_BLOCKING; and disable DQ outputs starting between tPAR_ALERT_ON and RL after the erroneous command and keep DQ outputs disabled until after tCMD_BLOCKING. This means that READ and MRR commands that were issued prior to the CA parity error may have all, some, or none of the typical DQS or DQ activity after tPAR_ALERT_ON. It is highly recommended that the host ignore read data on DQ after ALERT is asserted for a CA parity error in nonblocking mode. It is highly recommended that the host assert RESET_n when a CA parity error is detected in nonblocking mode.

In blocking mode only, if the PSD is not already in self-refresh mode, the DRAM shall internally issue PREab and SREREFabafter waiting PL + tRFCab, followed by SRE at least Max(tSR, tSRED) before tCMD_BLOCKING finishes. Similarly, the host may stop normal command sequences to all DRAMs that share the same ALERT pin, wait for all previous commands to be fully executed, and then issue PREab, REFab,and SRE commands to put the devices in a safe state after ALERT is detected and before (tCMD_BLOCKING × 80%)elapses.

In blocking mode only, if a CA parity error is detected and the CA Parity Recovery Mode mode register bit is 1b, then the DRAM shall copy the VREFCA shadow mode register value to the VREFCA normal mode register before tCMD_BLOCKING elapses.
In blocking mode only, after tCMD_BLOCKING, the DRAM shall automatically stop blocking commands from the host.

In blocking mode only, the host shall stop sending commands before (tCMD_BLOCKING × 80%) elapses. After (tCMD_BLOCKING × 120%), the DRAM is ready to accept commands for normal operation. Parity latency will be in effect and parity checking will resume immediately.

It is possible that the DRAM might have ignored a refresh command during the tCMD_BLOCKING window or the refresh command is the first erroneous frame, so it is recommended that the controller issues extra refresh cycles as needed.

The CA Parity Error Status mode register bit may be read any time by the host after(tCMD_BLOCKING× 120%), to determine which DRAM had the error. The DRAM maintains the CA Parity Error Log C0-C5 mode registers for the first erroneous command until the CA Parity Error Status mode register bit is reset to ‘0’.
